outlook: Grains bounced Friday morning after Thursday's losses, led by soybeans: January soybeans were up about 17 cents near $12.36, pushing to a new high for the week, helped by USDA's announcement Thursday of a 136,000-tonne soybean sale to China. December Minneapolis spring wheat was up about 8 cents to $6.31 and Chicago wheat gained 12 1/2 cents as wheat bounced off eight-month lows in oversold conditions, while December corn rose 6 cents to $4.48 1/2. A U.S. dollar near a 19-month high remains a headwind, and USDA's weekly export sales report, delayed a day by Veterans Day, was due this morning. ICE January canola was up about C$7.30 to C$784.60 per tonne; cash bids below are from Thursday's Minneapolis report.
